sections.h2: Where is the Mitchell County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 4, Bakersville, NC 28705, in the same administration complex as the Tax Assessor. Phone is 828.688.2139, extension 1402. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, and documents are recorded during those same hours.

Marriage certificates are issued from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The office's online services list covers deed search, vital records, an online vital request, marriage licenses, document recording standards, index standards, redaction of personal information, e-recording and fee schedules. Additional material is posted at mitchelldeeds.com.

In a county of 15,062 residents, one office handles the whole recording step for a house sale. Call ahead if a closing has a tight deadline.

sections.h2: What does the Mitchell County Register of Deeds record?
sections.html:
The office records deeds and other property documents, and it provides vital records, both current and historical, for birth, death and marriage. The county describes the office as a place for recording and research on deeds.

Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option, lease longer than three years or right of first refusal protects its holder against lien creditors and later buyers only from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies. For Mitchell County land, that means this office in Bakersville. Priority follows the order of registration, so two documents on the same parcel are ranked by the time each was recorded.

The register of deeds is elected every two years by county voters under G.S. 161-1.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Mitchell County?
sections.html:
North Carolina sets these fees statewide, so Mitchell County charges the same amounts as every other county. G.S. 161-10 prints $26.00 for the first 15 pages of an ordinary instrument and $64.00 for the first 35 pages of a deed of trust or mortgage, with $4.00 for each added page.

Recording fees under G.S. 161-10, collected in Mitchell County
DocumentFee printed in the statute
Instruments in general$26.00, first 15 pages
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00, first 35 pages
Each additional page$4.00
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each page after
Nonstandard document$25.00 added
Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive and says they are collected before filing. Ask the office for its current fee schedule page before you send a check.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Mitchell County house sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the duty on the transferor, who pays the register of deeds in the county where the property is located before the deed can be recorded. The rate is $1.00 for each $500 of the price or value, counting any fraction of $500 as a full unit.

One half stays in the county general fund. The other half goes to the Department of Revenue each month, less refunds and the county's 2 percent allowance on the state share. If the parcel spans two counties, the tax is paid in the county holding the greater value.

Your closing attorney will state the exact excise tax on the settlement statement for your price. Mitchell County's median owner-occupied home value is $220,100 for 2020 to 2024, according to the Census Bureau, and the figure for your own house depends only on the price in your deed.

sections.h2: How can an owner guard against deed fraud in Mitchell County?
sections.html:
Subscribe to the free Fraud Alert system on the Register of Deeds page. It notifies you if someone tries to change your property listings. Owners of vacant, rental or inherited houses benefit most, because nobody is watching the mail.

The county also lists a Redaction of Personal Information service. Ask the office what it covers and what form it requires.

  • Keep your own copy of every deed, satisfaction and release.
  • Check the index now and then for your name and parcel.
  • Record a deed of gift or inheritance document promptly instead of leaving it in a drawer.

Where a house is sold on a contract for deed, Chapter 47H applies to one-to-four family homes priced at $5,000 or more with five or more payments. The seller must record the contract or a memorandum of it within five business days, and the buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day.

sections.h2: How does recording fit with Mitchell County property tax?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds and the tax offices are separate, but a sale touches all of them. The deed goes to the register, while the tax bill is paid at the Tax Collector at 61 Crimson Laurel Circle. The county's tax collector reminds owners that bills mail in August to the owner of record as of January 1, so closing papers should show who covers the year.

State and county relief programs are filed with the Tax Assessor, not the register. The elderly or disabled exclusion uses Form AV-9, and the disabled veteran exclusion first needs a Veterans Service Officer to complete Form NCDVA-9. Both are described on the Mitchell County property tax page.

If you inherited a Mitchell County house, a cash buyer can close without repairs and handle recording through a closing attorney, so the title moves into the buyer's name on the day of settlement.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Mitchell County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 828.688.2139 and ask for extension 1402. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 4, Bakersville, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: How much is the state excise tax on a deed in Mitchell County?
faqs.a: It is $1.00 for every $500 of price or value, counting a fraction of $500 as a full unit. The seller pays it to the register of deeds before recording.

faqs.q: Does Mitchell County charge a fee to record a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 provides that satisfactions and cancellations of deeds of trust or mortgages are recorded without a fee.

faqs.q: Can I record documents electronically in Mitchell County?
faqs.a: The office lists E-Recording among its services. Contact the Register of Deeds at 828.688.2139, extension 1402, for the current process and any account requirements.

faqs.q: Why does the date and time of recording matter?
faqs.a: Because priority follows the order of registration. Under G.S. 47-18, an unrecorded conveyance or option does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies.
